Component: src/app/components/braid/braid.component.ts
Template: src/app/components/braid/braid.component.html
Styles: src/app/components/braid/braid.component.scss
Assets (SVGs): under src/assets/misc_braid_nvx_fkb/ (braid.svg, braid2.svg, …)
Geometry approach in that code:
The HTML defines a single large SVG with <defs> for all shapes (commas/arrows/rects/circle, gradients, filters). The braid is constructed by:
Drawing stacked “greenCircle” rings via a translated <use> of an id="circle" path.
Drawing link rectangles and arrows between rings via repeated <use> of rectV/rectHleft/rectHright and arrow/arrowL/arrowR shapes.
Drawing the inner yin-yan-like “comma” bubbles via leftCommaXL/rightCommaXL paths with text overlays for chord labels.
Angular loops use center_left, center_right, left_up, right_up, etc., from braid_tonalities.json and rotate arrays by tonality.
Interaction classes (active, erase, midi_active) set fill/stroke and filters.
Net: classic braid geometry is entirely defined by reusable <defs> and transforms on <use> elements with a fixed vertical spacing (translate(0, (i+1)90)).
Next steps I can do:
Port this exact SVG architecture to Harmonic Oracle:
Create a React component that embeds the same <defs> and replicates the ngFor loops as map() over the tonal arrays.
Use the same transforms and class names; replace Angular bindings with React props/state.

Preserve gradients/filters to match visuals.
